draft.text: You came in because you have pain on the inside of your right elbow that has been getting worse over the past four days.
You described the pain as a dull ache that can become sharp when you move your wrist or use your arm against resistance.
You have tenderness around the inside of your elbow, near the medial epicondyle, which is a bony part of the elbow.
The doctor will check your medications and may refer you to physical therapy.
You will need to rest your elbow and avoid activities that make the pain worse.
A follow-up appointment will be scheduled to check on your progress.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have been having pain on the inside of your right elbow for four days.
The pain gets worse when you move your wrist or do activities like pottery or lifting.
We found that you have tenderness around the inside of your elbow, specifically near the medial epicondyle.
There is no swelling, redness, or numbness in your elbow or forearm.
This may be a condition called medial epicondylitis, which is pain and tenderness on the inside of the elbow often caused by repetitive strain or overuse.
The doctor will check your medications and may refer you to physical therapy.
You should rest your elbow and avoid activities that make the pain worse.
A follow-up appointment will be scheduled to check on your progress.
